cio_brief.text: Good morning, Raj. Before the care team starts outreach, one thing needs your attention: the impactability model failed its subgroup check.

points: Frontier ZIPs rank 18% lower than similar town members; 57 high-need frontier members miss the top 300.
Also: the usual 45-day claims lag and low social needs coverage.

props.note: Synthetic data for a demo; every person and organization is fictional.

cio_subgroup.text: The model uses past utilization as a main input, so frontier members are ranked lower in every condition group.

points: Frontier members have 31% fewer primary care visits: a 74-minute median drive, and 190 have no broadband.
Fewer visits mean fewer claims, which the model reads as lower risk.
Same conditions and labs, ranked lower in every group: the known cost-as-proxy bias.

props.title: Average risk rank by condition group (percentile), frontier vs town

props.note: Synthetic data for a demo; every person and organization is fictional.

chips: What changes if we fix it?

cio_fix.text: Access-adjusted features bring the frontier gap from 18% to 3%, inside the release threshold.

points: 57 frontier members enter the top 300; 57 lower-need town members leave.
41 of the 57 are in the BP denominator, which helps the quality gate.

props.text: Sample of the 57 entering and 57 leaving the top 300, de-identified

props.note: Synthetic data for a demo; every person and organization is fictional.

cio_packet.text: Here is the governance packet: the updated model card, the subgroup results before and after, the feature change log and a sign-off page for you and Dr. Castellanos.

points: Until you sign, the care team sees the current ranking with a pending-fix banner.
Also drafted: ADT-based ED alerts to cover the 45-day claims lag.

chips: Send to Dr. Castellanos for co-sign

cio_signoff.text: Signed: the release now waits only on Dr. Castellanos's co-sign, and the care team keeps the pending-fix banner until then.
